title: The Grothendieck bottom edge computed on an augmented resolution comparison
statement: Let $A,B$ be Grothendieck abelian categories and $C$ an abelian category, all equipped with bounded below derived categories. Let $F:A\to B$ and $G:B\to C$ be additive left exact functors [def-sp-left-exact-additive], with $F$ sending injectives to $G$-acyclics. Let $X\in A$, let $I$ resolve $X$ and $J$ resolve $F(X)$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and let $\phi:J^\bullet\to F(I^\bullet)$ satisfy $\iota_J^0\phi^0=F(\iota_I^0)$. For every $n\in\mathbb N$, the canonical Grothendieck bottom edge [lem-sp-grothendieck-edge-maps] is the composite $R^nG(F(X))\xrightarrow{\rho_J}H^n(GJ)\xrightarrow{H^n(G\phi)}H^n(GFI)\xrightarrow{\rho_I^{-1}}R^n(GF)(X)$, where $\rho$ denotes the canonical right-derived resolution comparison [lem-sp-derived-well-defined]. No Ext or sheaf cohomology comparison is involved.

proof.text: Apply lem-sc-grothendieck-bottom-augmentation to identify the raw bottom edge, transported by the canonical F-resolution derived isomorphism, with H^n(RG(a_J)) followed by H^n(RG(Q phi)). This isolates only the augmentation/truncation step; it uses no composite acyclicity.

In private lemma bottom_resolution_map_unit, apply resolution_homology_transport for G and J. Naturality of extension homology and mapExtendIso moves the homology map of G(phi) through the extension comparisons. Naturality of homologyFunctorObjQIso and of the G derived unit then gives the same H^n(RG(a_J))H^n(RG(Q phi)) composite. The G unit on J is invertible because its terms are injective.

Prove the composite-unit transport privately for an arbitrary abelian C: the proof of lem-pc-canonical-resolution-composite-unit-comparison uses no injectives in C. Expand the composition isomorphism unit equation, use its naturality on the resolution augmentation, and cancel the F unit on I. Naturality through the map/extension comparison, followed by resolution_homology_transport for GF, gives bottom_resolution_composite_unit_transport. Cancel the abutment inverse followed by H^n(RG(e_F)), rewrite that transport, and combine the first two equalities. This is the original bottom-edge resolution formula with all hypotheses unchanged.

lean.statement: theorem grothendieckBottomEdgeMap_eq_resolution {A : Type uA} [Category.{vA} A] [Abelian A] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{vA} A] {B : Type uB} [Category.{vB} B] [Abelian B] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{vB} B] {C : Type uC} [Category.{vC} C] [Abelian C] [HasDerivedCategory A] [HasDerivedCategory B] [HasDerivedCategory C] (F : A ⥤ B) (G : B ⥤ C) [F.Additive] [G.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits F] [PreservesFiniteLimits G] (hFG : F.IsAcyclicComposablePair G) (X : A) (I : InjectiveResolution X) (J : InjectiveResolution (F.obj X)) (φ : J.cocomplex ⟶ (F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj I.cocomplex) (hφ : J.ι.f 0 ≫ φ.f 0 = F.map (I.ι.f 0)) (n : ℕ) : (F.grothendieckBottomEdgeMap G hFG n).app X = (J.isoRightDerivedObj G n).hom ≫ HomologicalComplex.homologyMap ((G.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).map φ) n ≫ (I.isoRightDerivedObj (F ⋙ G) n).inv
